editorial:
Imagine a family dinner where nobody is allowed to keep secrets anymore. That is the wild setup behind this French comedy-drama. After teenager Romain gets caught masturbating during biology class, his parents decide the whole family needs to talk openly about sex. What follows is a series of honest, funny, and sometimes awkward conversations between three generations. Grandparents, parents, and kids all share their desires and past experiences. The tone is light but surprisingly warm, and the film treats its subject with a mix of humor and heart. You will laugh at the awkward moments, but you may also feel touched by how the family grows closer.

The acting feels natural and relaxed, which helps the story land. Pacing is steady, though some scenes run a bit long. The biggest strength is how comfortable the film is with its topic, never judging anyone. On the downside, the humor can feel repetitive, and the plot is thin. If you enjoy European comedies that push boundaries, this one is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the family gathers after all the confessions. Romain, once embarrassed, now feels accepted. The grandparents reveal they still have an active love life, which shocks but inspires the younger members. The twist is that the biology teacher who caught Romain is connected to the family in an unexpected way, leading to one last awkward but funny moment. The film ends with everyone laughing together, showing honesty brought them closer. You are left feeling that open talk, even about uncomfortable topics, can heal family bonds.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves European comedies that push boundaries.
